label: WABAG
rationale: The Saudi Water Authority EPCC contract is firm and stated at about INR 2,700 crore, roughly 91% of TTM revenue of INR 2,965 crore, so the size test passes. It is not clearly beyond the company's disclosed history: the INR 4,400 crore Chennai 400 MLD DBO (March 2023) and a stream of INR 400-800 crore desalination and wastewater orders show that large orders are a regular flow for this company. The trigger's INR 60 billion firm figure is a preferred-bidder pipeline, so the event is rejected as routine; a reviewer who treats Saudi municipal work as a new market could reasonably move it to WATCH_MILESTONE.

Pre-existing earnings are strong (FY25 PAT INR 158 crore), and equity raised in the preferential issue, so no stress or fatal-flaw disqualifier applies.

label: DHRUV
rationale: The MSIDC letter of award is firm and its stated fee of Rs 23.46 crore over 90 months is 28.8% of FY24 revenue of Rs 81.50 crore (total against annual revenue, as the rules require; about 3.8% a year). It is not routine: the ticket is about 1.7x the largest contract disclosed before, and the company's typical awards were Rs 3-11 crore. The fee is for a consortium project, and the company's JV share is unstated, so the size is an upper bound that stays above 10% only if its share is at least about 35%. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable and has just completed an equity raise.

1. In our Critical Power business, received Advance Purchase Order of 1,680 Cr for supply of Hybrid Power systems, Li-ion based Energy storage and services for over 10 years from selected system integrators for Bharat Net Connectivity Project.
Early signs of recovery were visible in a recently secured landmark order worth ~INR 1680 crore, for supplying DC power and energy storage solutions for the BharatNet project over the next 3 years.

Starting with some of the key highlights, even before we go into Q3 results, we have had some really landmark events in the company, one of which is the receipt of the biggest purchase orders your company has ever received in its history of about Rs. 1,680 crores in our critical power business, which will include the scope of supply of hybrid power systems, lithium-ion batteries, and various kinds of services including annual maintenance contracts for over 10 years.

Some of this growth can be also attributed to PM e-drive policies, which brings certainty around the subsidy and incentives around electric vehicle ecosystem, launch of multiple new car models, and continuing e-bus deployment.
And Tritium has already received some good orders in last quarter, which is about roughly Rs. 13.7 million from 3, 4 large charging, deploying companies across the world.
We also announced MoU with two leading companies.
It's been just couple of weeks we have received maybe not even less than that, big orders in critical power.

label: EXICOM
rationale: The firm telco DC-power order of about INR 85 crore is 6.6% of TTM revenue of INR 1,277 crore (STATED); the 1,500 crore figure in the packet is backlog and does not size an event. Exicom wins telco orders of this size regularly (about 100 crore in Feb 2026, 113 crore in May 2026), so it is routine, but TTM operating margin of -7.1% (below 10%) and TTM revenue growth of 55.6% (above 0%) trigger the thin-margin exception, so it is judged as non-routine. Below the 10% threshold with a plausible path to material via repeated quarterly telco wins and a BSNL FY27 program, so WATCH_MILESTONE; no disqualifier, though the company is loss-making.

✓ Secured large order from Big telco’s for Lithium-ion batteries

We secured large orders from big telcos for lithium-ion batteries and this space is undergoing a shift of rapid transformation where large lithium-ion batteries are replacing traditional lead acid batteries.

Exicom -Colour palette Key Highlights – Q2 FY26 AC Charger Achieved highest ever sales of AC Charger by volume (20K+) and revenue Secured order for deployment in defense of 43 x 240 KW; 53 Nos of Bus / Truck Segment 240 kW for Delhi bus hubs; 50 x 240kW for Truck OEM DC Charger 100% migration of customers to Gen 2.0 platform 3kW Portable charger launched E Commerce In addition to already successful 7kW wallbox sales Successful collaboration to setup 180kW ultra fast chargers with end to end OEM End to End turnkey solution pan India Investor Presentation –Q2 FY26 10

We also secured orders from large telcos and tower companies for lithium-ion batteries as the trend of lead-acid conversion to lithium-ion continues to be strong.
• BESS – Breakthrough into a number of new accounts and secured initial orders (~$1Mn)marking our green energy entry

• Large purchase order secured for DC power systems from one of India’s biggest telecom from FY'27; executed multiple projects with the biggest Telco in Africa player andcontinued to grow our market share with established customers in DRC & Nigeria
On the AC charging side, Exicom won a 3-year contract with a leading passenger car manufacturer for its newly launched portable charger, Spin Free.

Additionally, Tritium has received a combination of purchase orders and forecasts totalling to ~USD 30 million from a large US-based customer for the current calendar year, the deliveries for which have already started from Jan 2026 onwards.
In Q3 FY26, aligned to this Telco expansion cycle, the business secured a large initial-phase DC power conversion systems order exceeding ~₹100 crore from one of India’s largest Telcos.

At Tritium, we bagged almost a $30 million combination of firm purchase order and forecast for high-speed DCEV charges from a large US customer, from one of the Fortune 50 US customers, with deliveries spread over full calendar year ‘26.
We continued execution for key system integrators who have won this contract, which includes RVNL, HFCL, NCC, and now we have secured formal from ITI as well.
Tritium’s next- generation DC-FLEX fleet charger secured orders from one of the largest US fleet operators, with deliveries expected to begin in CY 2027.
● Private Telecom Operator ○ Secured large DC Power Systems order worth ~₹113 Cr which is under execution; ○ Large volume to offset part of cost rise due to forex, commodity
